title: Entropy-driven probe generation and prioritization playbook
author: Marisol Alvarez
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes an entropy-driven workflow for generating, scoring, prioritizing, and sampling evaluation probes (short input prompts, dialog seeds, or workload traces) using live telemetry signals. The approach is designed to surface rare or unstable behaviors while balancing evaluation cost and annotation bandwidth. Use this playbook when you need continuous, targeted coverage of model failure modes, drifting slices, or capacity-sensitive corners of production traffic.

Goals:
- Discover high-utility probes from production telemetry with minimal human effort.
- Prioritize probes that maximize information about model regressions (quality delta), quantization sensitivity, and latency anomalies.
- Provide deterministic scoring and an auditable pipeline from telemetry to evaluator-runbooks.

When to use this playbook:
- Integrating new model variants into Dedicated/Private canaries.
- Creating targeted prompt sets to stress quantized variants or KV-cache behavior.
- Triaging intermittent production regressions where labeled examples are scarce.

Definitions and components:
- Probe: A single input example (prompt + metadata) used in an eval job.
- Probe Farm: service name "probe-farm" (k8s: namespace eval-tools) that stores candidate probes in ClickHouse (table: probes.catalog).
- Eval Orchestrator: "eval-orchestrator" that schedules evaluator-sdk jobs and reports results to the eval-metrics topic in Kafka.
- Telemetry signals: metrics and logs sourced from prod (Prometheus, traces, and structured logs forwarded to ClickHouse/Clickhouse-materialized views).

Signal taxonomy and mapping (table):
| Signal name             | Source         | Frequency | Interpretation                                      | Weight (default) |
|-------------------------|----------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| token-error-rate        | eval-metrics   | 1m        | Token-level hallucination/safety sentinel hits     | 0.30             |
| response-entropy        | probes.agg     | 5m        | High entropy = diverse/confused outputs            | 0.20             |
| lat99                  | prometheus     | 1m        | 99th percentile latency for model route            | 0.10             |
| kv-cache-miss-rate      | prod-kv-metrics| 1m        | Cold starts and cache eviction sensitivity         | 0.10             |
| user-friction-score     | product-telemetry | realtime| Product-derived signal (errors, retries, cancels)  | 0.20             |
| annotation-gap-score    | probe-farm     | on-demand | Low historical labels for this workload slice      | 0.10             |

Scoring and prioritization algorithm (high level):
1) Candidate extraction: pull candidate inputs from prod trace windows using producers: structured-log extractor, trace-sampler, and request-diff job. Default window: last 72 hours. Query examples:
   - ClickHouse: SELECT request_id, prompt, session_id, route, model FROM prod.requests WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 72 hour AND route IN ('chat', 'completion') AND tokens > 8 LIMIT 200000;
2) Enrich candidates: join telemetry signals (token-error-rate, response-entropy, lat99, kv-cache-miss-rate, user-friction-score) into the candidate row.
3) Compute raw priority score:
   priority_raw = sum(w_i * normalized(signal_i)) - penalty(privacy, pii, customer_sensitive)
   where normalized(signal_i) uses rolling 7-day z-score bounded to [0,1].
4) Diversity adjustment: apply an embedding-based de-duplication (service: probe-farm/embed-index) that attenuates score for near-duplicates within the last 30 days using cosine similarity threshold 0.85.
5) Cost gating: apply heuristics to limit high-cost probes (length > 4096 tokens or multimodal attachments) unless explicitly labeled as high-priority.
6) Final priority buckets: HOT (top 0.5%), WARM (0.5%-5%), COLD (remaining).

Sampling and resampling policy:
- HOT probes: sample 100% into nightly evaluator runs (priority queue). Annotate with reason codes (e.g., TOKEN_ERR_SPIKE, HIGH_ENTROPY, KV_EVICT).
- WARM probes: sample 5% daily with stratified sampling across routes and customers (by tenant-hash).
- COLD probes: reservoir sample 0.05% weekly for long-tail drift detection.
- Resampling rule: if HOT probe receives a failing eval result (quality delta > regression threshold), clone and expand neighborhood by retrieving 50 nearest embedding neighbors and promote top-10 by rescored priority.

Annotation schema and labeling contract:
- label: {"category": string, "severity": one of [critical, major, minor], "notes": string, "annotator": string, "timestamp": ISO8601}
- Required fields: category, severity, annotator. Optional: customer_consent_id if sample contains customer-provided content.
- Labeler SLA: initial triage within 48h for HOT probes; 7 days for WARM. Use the "annotate-probe" internal UI (path: /tools/probe-annotator).

Privacy and safety gating:
- PII detection: run pii-scanner (lambda) at extraction time. Any probe with PII flag set must be redacted or moved to restricted bucket and requires security review (owner_team: security).
- Customer-sensitive sampling: probes tagged tenant_sensitive are only eligible for Private/Dedicated shadow evals when customer opt-in exists.

Integration with eval harness and CI/CD:
- Eval job naming: entropy-probe-YYYYMMDD-{bucket}
- Example CI trigger (GitOps):
  curl -X POST "https://eval-orchestrator.internal/api/v1/run" -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_TOKEN" -d '{"job": "entropy-probe-20260212-HOT", "model": "rwd-1.3-quantized-v2", "probe_source": "probe-farm:HOT"}'
- Result consumer: eval-orchestrator writes to Kafka topic eval-results; a consumer (eval-ingest) populates eval-results.clickhouse and alerts via ops-alerts when regression_count >= 3 for a model variant.

Canary gating and rollout policy (recommended):
1) Run nightly HOT evals against both float and quantized candidates.
2) If a critical category regression is detected (delta > 0.08 in task-level accuracy or safety-sentinel spike > 2x baseline), block canary rollout and trigger regression triage playbook (see related pages).
3) For non-critical but actionable regressions, schedule a focused micro-canary (2k qps shadow) and run expanded probe neighborhoods.

Operational runbook (incident-light):
- Owner: applied-ml/evals team oncall (primary: @applied-evals)
- If probe pipeline stops producing HOT candidates for >24h:
  1. Check probe-farm deployment status: kubectl -n eval-tools get pods -l app=probe-farm
  2. Validate ClickHouse connectivity and recent ingestion: SELECT count(*) FROM probes.catalog WHERE created_at >= now() - INTERVAL 1 hour;
  3. Check telemetry ingestion: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group telemetry-collector
- If scoring anomalies (scores all zero): check z-score windowing job (cron: score-normalizer) and restart: kubectl -n eval-tools rollout restart deployment/score-normalizer

Metrics, SLOs and dashboards:
- Metric: HOT probe discovery rate — SLI target: 1000 HOT candidates/day (SLO: 95% monthly).
- Metric: annotation turnaround for HOT probes — SLO: 48h 95th percentile.
- Metric: regression detection lag — time from first failing prod example to HOT promotion — SLO: < 24h 90th percentile.
- Dashboards: Grafana dashboard id: eval-entropy-001 (panels for signal distribution, HOT arrival rate, and annotation backlog).

Example JSON candidate (stored in probes.catalog):
{
  "probe_id": "pf-20260212-000123",
  "prompt": "Write a short explanation of differential privacy in simple terms.",
  "route": "completion",
  "tokens": "48",
  "response_entropy": "0.88",
  "token_error_rate": "0.032",
  "kv_cache_miss": "0.12",
  "priority_raw": "0.78",
  "priority_bucket": "HOT",
  "extraction_window": "2026-02-12T03:14:00Z"
}

FAQ (short):
Q: How do we avoid overfitting probes that repeatedly fail for the same annotate pattern?
A: We decay priority for probes that have stable failing labels beyond a half-life of 21 days and upweight neighbors instead.

Q: Can product teams request targeted probes?
A: Yes. Submit to /tools/probe-requests with tenant, route, and rationale. Requests are treated as manual HOT promotions after security review.
